content: It is currently unknown whether rifapentine is excreted into breast milk. However, similar medications are known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. It is important to maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Rifapentine may accelerate the elimination of other medications from your body, potentially reducing their effectiveness. This medication may also decrease the efficacy of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in unintended pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use additional reliable birth control methods while taking this medication. Rifapentine may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as those measuring folate and vitamin B12 levels, potentially leading to inaccurate test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and medical tests, such as sputum tests, liver function tests, bilirubin levels, and complete blood counts, should be conducted regularly. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as prescribed. If you miss a dose and remember on the same day, take it as soon as you remember. If you remember the missed dose the next day or later, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a revised dosing schedule. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or headache. Rifapentine may cause bodily fluids, such as urine, sweat, saliva, or tears, to turn a reddish color. This effect is harmless and will resolve once the medication is discontinued. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacterium called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking rifapentine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other rifamycins (such as rifampin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Alcohol consumption may increase the risk of liver disease. Rifapentine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. If taken during the last few weeks of pregnancy, it may increase the risk of bleeding in both the mother and the infant. Notify your doctor immediately if you observe any bleeding in your newborn.
